I just unclip it and unroll the top and I'm able to fit my harness, shoes and the rest of my gear pretty easily. There are 2 side bottle holders which is great for keeping my water bottle. It holds everything I need.

For those looking for something to carry a laptop, the inside of this has a laptop sleeve. Also, the front zipper easily holds pens or pencils.

The fabric seems water resistant and somewhat sturdy, though not as good quality as some of the other backpacks I've had. There is padding on the inside where the pack sits up against the back. This helps with comfort. Overall, this is a decent, basic backpack.

reviews.title: While the waterproofing is an undeniable help, I can’t understand the hype of tuck backpacks?
reviews.text:
+ Waterproof
+ Exact coloration as advertised

± Very large, making it awkward on my small frame
± Flimsy plastic clasp; feels weak - as if stress will break it

- Despite appearing large, you can’t fit too much without the backpack appearing awkward (more on this later)
- Hard to place water bottles in when there are contents inside

---------------------------------

I wanted to like this bag, but there are some design flaws that definitely need to be looked at before I can. I’ve noticed the hype surrounding these “tuck” backpacks, but I can’t justify the hype at this price and with these functions.

First off, I do like that this backpack is waterproof. It provides a great peace of mind when protecting my laptop and other valuables, and I don’t have to worry about any contents getting wet. I don’t think this is a good enough reason, however, when an umbrella would suffice to keep myself - and contents - dry. Why do I say this?

Well, I don’t have a good way of explaining this, so hopefully the pictures I took do my attempt justice. My current gripe with the backpack is with how much you can fit in it - or really, lack of how much you can fit in it. As it stands, my other…

reviews.title: Small/Compact, Boxy Shape, Only One Compartment,
reviews.text:
This Amazon Basics backpack is your typical every day backpack. While it may be an everyday backpack, I would not recommend it for school. It can barely hold a few textbooks. It's more of a fashion bag. It really only has one main compartment which will really fit 3 notebooks (or 2 binders) and a laptop. It's actually very compact. You cannot hold much in there.
The looks are much better than the amount it can carry, honestly. The look of this bag is a very boxy and square shape. It doesn't really look nice from the back but if you like to change up your style, it's not a bad option because it's affordable enough to get you into the fashion game.
It has an interesting design however- it's water resistant to a certain degree, has one small extra pocket on the front for maybe a phone charger and a few writing utensils.
Here is what I use it for:
-Carrying a phone charger
-Carrying a Nintendo Switch w/ case
-Galaxy S4 Tablet
-Water bottle

With those few items, my bag is pretty much nearly full and if it becomes more full, it will push against my back and get really uncomfortable.
This backpack has a very simple design and is decent for everyday use, but don't expect to store a 15"…

reviews.title: The problem with backpacks
reviews.text: The main problem with backpacks is they are not designed for doing something active. I have a awesome Timbuk2 backpack that I love but it really doesn't work for long rides. This really isn't a commuter backpack. The inside compartment maybe could be stuffed with a change of clothes (activewear) but not really business work clothes and shoes, just a bit small. This is ideal for longer rides. The back has an extra deep cushion channel to keep it off your back. It's also very low profile. Ideally, I'm using this for extra tubes, tools, food, ID, phone, binoculars, book, etc. So the color looks better in-person than the pictures and has a clip for a light. Sort of the normal layout of a large compartment with smaller elastic compartment in the back. In the front, there is a quick access compartment at the top with a larger compartment with smaller mesh ones at the bottom. The zippers are not YKK but construction is quite good, much better than I expected. Most importantly, it looks pretty good and is something that I would easily use when I needed something for long rides. I rather do this than have a bike rack/panniers on my gravel bike. No extra weight on bike and don't have to…

reviews.title: Lightweight and comfortable
reviews.text: This backpack is great when I'm going for rides and don't need to carry my bike lock. (When I need to carry a lock, I like to use a bag with a stiff back so that my back doesn't get poked by anything if things shift out of place, even though that bag is a bit heavier.) I like this bag for when I am going for a round-trip ride. It's very light and has pockets where I can put my phone, keys, water bottle, and jacket. I like the straps that hold it steady at both the chest and waist. It's comfortable, slim, very light, and has all the features I need.

reviews.title: No Bike Baskets? No PROBLEM!
reviews.text:
It is really light weight - but still has some padding between you and your cargo (in spots). Great for day-trips, might be a bit small for a multi-day adventure (but if you packed really light...).

Some breath-ability helps with having a pack on your back while you are pumping the pedals hard. You could place your hydration setup in this bag as well.

Price as reviewed seems maybe a bit on the high side, but it is nice.

reviews.title: Nice little day hiking backpack
reviews.text: I'm using this as a day hiking backpack. It's great for some snacks, supplies, and water, without being so big it's cumbersome. The back features both chest and waist straps and a padded back which means you can be fairly active without it bouncing around. Pocket configuration is basic but adequate for most uses. It lacks a water bottle side pocket but overall it's a nice value backpack for outdoor use.

Has compartment for camel pack, which makes the bag great for biking and hiking. Boyfriend is going to use as his work bag, but he is 6'1 and 230lbs...it looks like he borrowed my 8 year old's bag. He assures me, he likes it.

reviews.title: Visibility is best feature
reviews.text: The color combination can be seen well, even in low light, which gives visibility to a biker. There is room for a hydration bladder. This pack is also well suited for school.

reviews.title: Lean backpack solution without kindergarten feels
reviews.text:
Seems pretty good. I've ordered 2 different backpacks to compare, so this has not been used beyond opening. Translated: I cannot comment on durability-over-time or personal experience with this backpack.

Very, very lean design. I can see how this would be useful for cyclists or people needing to keep their center of gravity in tight spaces. I'm using this for general travel, and I didn't want a bulky backpack to cram under the airplane seat in front of me.

It's longer than the 2 different bags I have coming in soon. I'm a big/tall guy (6'-4") with a longer torso, so all too often backpacks make me look like I'm going to kindergarten.. This backpack, not so much. THEREFORE, give it a second look, if you are vertically challenged (i.e., short).

I could see this as a very useful commuter back, navigating heavy foot traffic scenarios, and-- let's be real-- secured on your back if you had to sprint through an airport. 😅

FREE TIP: Always wear running shoes when flying. Add a lean backpack to your list, too.

Feels very sturdy. I slung it on and snapped the high and low front buckles.. certainly effective. Everything's adjustable.

Colors are true to the image.. not too flashy, not…

reviews.title: Hard to see inside bag.
reviews.text:
This backpack seems to be made of water proof/water resistant material.
Each side has a drink pocket that are a little tight. They work fine for a purchased bottle of water.
The front has a zippered pocket that is hard to see - I like that for security.
The back has a padded laptop area. There is also a hole for stringing headphone cables through.
The back of the bag has a fully padded zippered area. This fits my iPad mini with some room to spare.
There is also a strap that would work for holding a jacket.
The shoulder straps are thickly padded.
There are 3 elastic loops on each shoulder strap to clip different things.
All of that is good.
The thing I don’t like about the bag is that the top opening is hard to use to navigate inside the main compartment.
I wish the zipper went the other direction.
It’s very dark inside the bag.
Thankfully the side of the bag has a zipper which helps to get across to the pockets inside the main area.

reviews.title: Lots of pockets, but when opening from the top it’s one big dark hole.
reviews.text:
I looked up “origami backpacks” and there was nothing - seems it’s not an actual thing. I think it’s called that because the top flips over (like origami folds) and slips closed with a hook.

I’m not sure if this is water resistant. It seems it would be, but I can’t be sure with the information available to me as of this writing. There are plenty of pockets, including one for your laptop - no USB connection though.

My main problem with it is I think it would be a genuine pain to use. When the top is unfolded and opened, you’re basically looking down into a long, narrow, black hole. And most of the pockets inside are at the bottom. Without a flashlight, a keen memory, or you’re willing to just use your sense of touch, I think it would be difficult to find much of anything, except by luck. There are zippers on either side, and that makes it easier to open the backpack, but they’re not wide enough. It’s not like it opens like a bag. You’d still have to do a bit of searching around, messing up your packing along the way, and I’m pretty positive that I’d always open the wrong side to find what I’m looking for.

It’s useless to me because I’m not into that level of aggravation. I’ll…

reviews.title: Really Durable Construction, Unusual Pocket Configuration
reviews.text:
This backpack is much like a headset that I reviewed where I wish there was another brand that Amazon could use outside of AmazonBasics. I consider AmazonBasics to be value or commodity items, but this backpack is much better designed than a basic one, and is of a premium quality unexpected in AmazonBasics products (most of them are as basic as the brand applies).

This backpack is more for outdoors than for laptop carriage. The pockets are really meant more for tools than for accessories. The outside is nylon and fairly weather-resistant. This can probably carry about 20 to 30 pounds successfully without ripping based on the way the base holds.

There are two pockets, but they are unusually designed, and I am not sure my photos do this justice. There is a laptop-like back pocket that is heavily padded, however, I would not put a laptop in that area. The reason why is that there is an open flap where the elements can get into the bag which would not be a good idea for anything electronic. The second pocket is the origami pocket with restricted entry from the top origami part and a side zipper opposite the drink holder. This has the utility pockets but also space for clothes or…

reviews.title: Nice bag disguised as a cheap bag ...
reviews.text:
If I don't find what I'm about to say is true, I'll return and update my review. But wow! I will admit right off the bat that I did not want to buy this bag. I had other bags in mind for the gym. However, I also have a very tight budget due to a certain virus **cough! cough!** (Too soon? Sorry!) reviews.title: Nice backpack
reviews.text:
This is a really nice, modern looking backpack. It's a soft olive green, the lines are sleek and simple, and there is one external pocket that is in line with the rest of the backpack. Inside it has plenty of space for up to a 15 inch, maybe larger laptop. 1 expandable pocket, which could be used for a laptop, has no padding.

OneNote, the word prism that's used in the title for this backpack is misleading. Generally speaking, prism these days refers to a light reflecting quality that is not present in his backpack. So know that before you buy it for that quality.

reviews.title: Really nice olive green backpack
reviews.text: This is a very light backpack. I love the color and the modern-day look to it. I think it's decent quality for the price so overall I am happy with this olive green backpack.

reviews.title: Light but sturdy
reviews.text:
This is a very simple, light backpack that actually expands a bit at the bottom to hold more than what it appears capable of initially. Inside the backpack at the back there is a pouch with elastic at the top with a picture of shoes on it, and indeed the pouch is spacious enough for a pair of shoes. There is another pouch (without elastic at the top) inside at the front for other items. Similarly, on the sides of the inside of the backpack there is one pouch with elastic at the top and one without. The one without shows a picture of a cell phone. The one with elastic could fit a water bottle.

On the outside of the backpack, there is only one zippered pouch on the front. It is fairly deep so it could accommodate a larger wallet. On the back of the backpack there is a strap for hooking onto a luggage handle.

The color is a nice army green.

reviews.title: functional backpack for short commutes
reviews.text:
This backpack is a bright army green color (if that makes sense. It’s like a shade of olive that is brighter than a typical olive.) Its the standard backspace size and inside has a padded back so you can safely transport a laptop. The straps are adjustable but are not padded, it’s relatively comfortable on though and I don’t think I’d complain about the non padded straps unless I was wearing it for more than standard commute. Inside also has a pocket with a little shoe image I guess it’s a shoe pocket? However if you put shoes in there you wouldn’t have much room in the pack for other items.
Overall I like this backpack OK. It’s functional but not very stylish.

reviews.title: I LOVE this backpack!
reviews.text:
Truth is ... I bought this backpack for its price but I love love love it! And, quite a few people have commented on it and asked me where I got it.

The color is really nice, it is sturdy, and holds everything I need. I am using a knee scooter right now while I recover from surgery from a broken ankle, and I use the backpack to carry whatever I need. It is sturdy enough to be secure on my back while scootering but comfortabe (and stylish) enough to be part of my work day!

I am so happy I bought this backpack! I will prob continue to use it even after I finish healing and dont use the scooter! You need a backpack that will make you happy, too!

reviews.title: not extremely light weight
reviews.text: This is an attractive, well made backpack. The back of the sack is well-padded and rigid enough that the backpack can stand on its own even when empty. There is a strap across the back which can be used to attach it to the handle of a roller bag. The only exterior compartment is a zippered pocket mid-front. there are multiple pockets on the inside; large front and back pockets and pockets on both sides nicely sized for bottles, umbrella, etc. The slightly rigid bottom of the bag is smaller than many bags, just about 6in wide equating to a less roomy interior. Overall, a pretty nice bag.

reviews.title: Now changed to US sizing; Size 9 runs large; Grid decoration on top
reviews.text:
The listings for the early reviews were mixed up in various ways, but that's been fixed now. The sizes listed are US sizes.

I usually wear a 9.5 or 10, but I noticed that at the UK site (which I checked to see what size I was really ordering--the ASIN numbers are the same) these were said to run large, and particularly the UK size 8 (EU 42), which is US size 9, so I ordered the 9. Sure enough, they fit very nicely, if snuggly with my thick winter socks. With thin socks they're roomy.

As can be seen in some of the Amazon photos, the top middle suede section has a diagonal grid of holes poked into it. It's decoration, they don't go through the leather. There's no color added, the light spots in the photos are light reflections.

The insoles are padded, stiffly and thinly except at the heel, which has a raised softer padding. There's also some light padding at the front half inside on the tops and sides.

Very mild arch support. The insoles are glued in, so it might be tricky to replace them.

The outsoles are medium-hard silicone-type rubber. They're dark but actually translucent. The tread pattern gives good traction and some of it is deep enough to last a little while.

reviews.title: Great lightweight backpack
reviews.text: At first glance this backpack seems pretty simple. It is very lightweight and seems to be made of a vinyl/poly material. It is very lightweight yet very durable. The material is thin but strong and waterproof. The material makes it light in weight and thus take up little space. It weighs barely nothing and only takes on what you put in it. It also surprisingly has more pockets and slots than it first looks like the same as a much bulkier backpack. It is very comfortable to wear and both the strap and the back of the pack has a thick, soft and durable mesh that will keep your back from getting sweaty when wearing it. At first look I honestly thought it was just an inexpensive backpack that wouldn't get much use. Instead it ends up getting heavy use and I highly recommend.

reviews.title: Excellent lightweight backpack!
reviews.text:
Excellent lightweight backpack!
By my scale this pack only weighs in at about 8 ounces yet features a few add ons that greatly improve functionality.
The shock cord webbing on the front of the pack allows you to store a rain coat or sweatshirt for when the weather turns for the worse.
A mesh pocket on one side for a water bottle or quick phone access.
A smaller, interior flap pocket could be used to store a small hydration bladder or smaller, valuable items that may get lost in the main body of the pack.
Mesh and padding on the shoulder straps and back of the pack provide a bit of comfort and ventilation.
For the price, a great value!

reviews.title: The Cheapest Backpack I've Ever Used
reviews.text:
Only really need one word to describe this backpack - cheap.

Everything about this backpack is cheap. The materials are so thin, I'm worried how well they will hold up. The shoulder straps are really weak and the zippers scare me.

There is an inside pocket and a somewhat breathable mesh on the back. Those are about the only real options.

At the time of this review, a price was not disclosed. If it's over $20 I'd have a hard time finding any value in it.

I guess the biggest concern is the durability. I'm almost afraid to take this out on a trail. My fear is it would fail in the middle of the hike.

reviews.title: Great catch all / light hiking backpack / or extra diaper bag
reviews.text:
This bag feels like a raincoat and “blue tarp” had a baby. The material appears as if it is waterproof (ish), I haven’t used it in wet weather to say for 100% if it would keep everything completely dry. The mesh back is not open to the interior. I would assume that this is more of a protective thing, if you were wearing this bag directly on your skin it would either stick to you or you would develop sores from the material rubbing, I believe the fabric mesh would stop that.
Lots of pockets and storage spots in the bag, can fit a lot of items in this. The shoulder straps are VERY comfortable. You could use this as a light weight book bag and be very comfortable in it. As packaged without adjusting straps bag went on easy, resting below my waist line, sitting on my butt. I am 5’9”, still have a lot of room to extend straps for larger or smaller size. There is not a mid-chest strap that clips / fastens in the front. While you can wear this in front of you, it will ride low.

One thing that COULD BE an issue is the bottom of the bag. This is the area that (for me) tends to break down the most quickly. Of course, this is the area of any bag that takes the most abuse and usually wears…

First compartment has a very deep channel that goes down and under the bag, deceivingly large. It also has two elastic mesh pockets and a zippered pouch behind (the size of the two mesh pockets), great for stuffing sunglasses, flashlights, tools, phones, etc.

Main compartment has an open pouch, about half the size of the bag. Good to keep items you don't want to fall to the bottom like snacks or tool or electronics. The main compartment is a decent size (30L) large enough to fit a large laptop, even though there is no padding for one. I stuffed size 12 sneakers, a hoodie, tshirt and full medical kit with enough room for a few more items.

reviews.title: I don’t hate these
reviews.text: These pointy slingback flats are most definitely not ballet flats. They are a tolerable option for the most dressy occasions when I would normally break out my lone pair of high heels. I normally wear a 9 or 9.5, and a 9 in these is fine in length. The functional buckles on the narrow back strap allow for some adjustments to improve this aspect of fit. The little toe of my left foot is a bit squished in where the toe box starts tapering to a point, but that’s always a risk with this sort of style. The footbed is minimally padded, and the sole is quite stiff. Traction isn’t great: while the textured grooves on the plastic bottom of the 1” heel offer a bit of grip, the remainder of the sole is slick despite some siping on the ball of the foot. Overall, these are nice looking and not so uncomfortable that I dread wearing them, although I am happy to kick them off when done.

reviews.title: Not at great as these reviews would lead you to believe.
reviews.text:
First and foremost, the "great arch support" review is either a wildly inaccurate mistake or a straight up lie. These shoes legitimately feel like you are walking on two separated soles, both with minimal padding. I, too, have flat feet, and guess what's in the most pain within 20min...yep, my arches/mid-foot. They feel like they're being stretched between two unconnected soles.

The soles themselves are bricks too. No padding, give, or bounce whatsoever...which is terrible for "walking shoes". The "memory foam" insoles are a joke too--they're too thin to matter, and I feel like Sketchers knows that. Additionally, they weren't "true to size" for me. I wear 10.5W, and these actually feel wider/larger than most shoes I get.

You're going to have to end up buying some nice insoles/inserts to make these shoes worth wearing daily, so you may as well just go ahead and buy a better shoe in the first place.

reviews.text: I thought hubs would love these shoes but he said he already has a pair like this and insisted I take them since they fit my ladies 11 size feet. reviews.title: Well sewn wallet with stiff backing
reviews.text:
Heaye Small Wallet for Women has a textured black surface that doesn’t show fingerprints. It is not labeled but feels like polyurethane. It is well sewn.

It has a 2.25” wide strap that uses a snap closure and is accented with a gold tone design that has a 1.125” diameter. The snap closure can be a bit tricky and I would like it better with a magnetic closure.

The wallet itself measures 3.5” x 4.5” and weighs 2.8 ounces. It is not a flexible wallet since there are firm cardboard like pieces built into each of the sides. It does not lay flat when open.

It holds bills and several cards neatly but there is no zipper section as currently mentioned on the product page.

This Heaye Small Wallet is an attractive and functional small wallet that will hold the basics. The strap closure with a gold tone accent gives it a fashionable look.

reviews.title: Perfectly adequate

A very simplistic wallet with a textured body and a snap closure. There's a round, golden design on the snap that's very elegant and pretty, but the snap itself is a smidge difficult to get together. There's room enough for 5 cards and a picture or I.D. as well as cash, but there's no zipper or additional pocket for change. It's nice enough for a temporary wallet, but I wouldn't use it longterm, both because of the lack of a zipper pocket and no RFID protection.
It doesn't look or feel like leather, but it has a nice feel to it anyway and seems relatively sturdy. It's simple, but not in a bad way. You get what you buy for, which is a perfectly adequate wallet.
